edit.new: - Anchor only the **main event** of a sentence to `document-creation-time` (or to a time expression of its clause). Attach every other event of the sentence to that main event or to a nearby event, usually `:overlap` (`:contained` if it lies inside it, `:before`/`:after` when the order is clear). Ev...

edit.old: an ordinary classifier (个, 本, 只, 位) is dropped (三本书 → `书 :quant 3`).
edit.new: a classifier is kept as the unit too, including 个, 份, 款, 本 (一份小报 → `小报 :quant 1 :unit (份)`).

edit.anchor: Chinese names are split into words, not characters: 欧洲议会 → `:op1 "欧洲" :op2 "议会"`.
edit.text: In Chinese names keep the title brackets 《 》 as their own `:opN` (《世界新闻周报》 → `:op1 "《" :op2 "世界" ... :opN "》"`). Do not add `:wiki` in Chinese documents. A country or place name that modifies a noun (美国小报) is `:place`, not `:mod`. Do not corefer a repeated country name that is only such a modifier.

When the text has a lexical verb that is in Chinese PropBank (属, 拥有), use that verb with its frame's roles instead of `belong-91` / `have-91`. Superlatives and comparatives (最, 更, *most, more*) use `(have-degree-91 :ARG1 X :ARG2 <property> :ARG3 (最))`, not `:degree`.

edit.new: *but* (但是, 却, 然而, 不过, 可是) `but-91`;
*because* (因为, 由于) and 以…而 → `:reason`;

edit.anchor: A discontinuous word (帮……忙) is one concept aligned to its span.
edit.text: A fixed four-character idiom is one concept. A pair of coordinated nouns written together (奇闻轶事) is split: `(and :op1 (奇闻) :op2 (轶事))`.

- Chinese adverbs are concepts, not only aspect cues. 已经, 都, 也, 仍, 还 and 其中 → `:mod (<word>)`; 曾经 → `:temporal (曾经)`. A medium (电视, 网络) is `:medium`.
- A modifier shared by coordinated nouns goes on each conjunct by reentrancy, never on the `and` node.
- Do not add arguments (agents, possessors) t...

edit.anchor: | `process` | an event nominal, or a process whose type cannot be told (*the meeting*, 探索 as a noun) |
edit.text: Aspect cues: recurring activities of a publication or institution (发行, 报导, 综合) are `habitual`, even with 了. 已经 + 停止 or another end verb used to describe an entity is `state` (the resulting state). Passive naming (被称为) is `performance`.
